title: E-Commerce Boutique: ROAS 1.2 vs Target 3.0
story: A D2C apparel brand selling ethnic kurtas is spending ₹20,000/day. Their ROAS is 1.2x (unprofitable), while their target breakeven is 3.0x. You are brought in to identify where the money is leaking.

steps.prompt: Analyzing the funnel metrics above, where is the primary leak occurring?
options: In the ad creative and hook (CTR is bad)
In the ad auction CPM (inventory too expensive)
At the website checkout: Visitors are adding items to cart enthusiastically, but abandoning at checkout
steps.explain: CTR is 2.3% (fantastic) and Add-to-Cart is 8.5% (healthy). But only 1.1% of cart additions turn into purchases, indicating checkout friction.

steps.prompt: You inspect the checkout page on a mobile device. What common issues would cause this checkout collapse in India?
options: High unexpected shipping fees added at final step, lack of Cash-on-Delivery (COD) or UPI checkout options, and slow loading payment gateway
The font size is 14px instead of 16px
The brand's Instagram handle has no blue checkmark
steps.explain: In Indian e-commerce, unexpected delivery charges at the last step, missing Cash on Delivery, or broken UPI gateways cause 80%+ of checkout drop-offs.

finalQuestion: In under 80 words, state the 3 recommendations you will give the brand founder to reach 3.0x ROAS.
keyPoints: Fix checkout friction: Add 1-click UPI and Cash on Delivery (COD)
Remove unexpected shipping charges at checkout or offer free shipping over ₹999
Deploy a dedicated 0-7 day Cart Abandoner retargeting sequence
modelAnswer:
1. Eliminate unexpected ₹150 shipping charges at the final step by building delivery into product pricing or offering free shipping above ₹999.
2. Enable 1-click UPI checkout and verified Cash-on-Delivery (COD) with OTP verification.
3. Launch a dedicated 0-7 day Bottom-of-Funnel retargeting campaign on Meta with customer reviews and a 10% abandoned cart discount code.
